in_arabic.name: خارجة
in_arabic.meaning: الولادة أو الخروج من الرحم أو مكان ما
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم خارجة مشتق من الجذر العربي 'خ-ر-ج' والذي يحمل معاني الخروج أو الخروج من مكان ما. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران الآية ١٢٦ 'وَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي' حيث يشير إلى الخروج في سبيل الله. في الثقافة الإسلامية، يرمز الاسم إلى الشجاعة والاستقلال.

in_urdu.name: خارجہ
in_urdu.meaning: خروج کرنا یا رحم سے پیدائش
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام خارجہ عربی جڑ 'خ-ر-ج' سے نکلا ہے جس کے معنی ہیں باہر نکلنا یا کسی جگہ سے نکلنا. قرآن مجید میں سورة آل عمران کی آیت ١٢٦ میں 'وَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي' کا ذکر ہے جو اللہ کی راہ میں نکلنے کی بات کرتا ہے. جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں، یہ نام بہادری اور آزادی کی علامت ہے.

in_pashto.long_meaning: د خارجة نوم etymology د عربي ريښو 'خ-ر-ج' څخه دي چې د معنی يې د يو ځای څخه وتل یا بيرون تګ دي. په قران کريم کې، سورة آل عمران آيت ١٢٦ 'وَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي' د الله په لاره کې د وتلو خبرې کوي. د افغان او پښتون دود، دا نوم د زړورتیا او آزادۍ نښه ده.

in_english.name: Kharijaht
in_english.meaning: Going out, being born, or coming out of a place
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kharijaht originates from the Arabic root 'خ-ر-ج' (kharaja), meaning 'to go out' or 'to exit'. This root is mentioned in the Quran, Surah Al Imran, Verse 126, indicating exiting or going out for the sake of Allah. The name symbolizes courage, independence, and sometimes spiritual emergence. Across Muslim cultures, Kharijaht signifies a strong and determined personality.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kharijaht" (pronounced khah-ree-jah-th) has historical and cultural significance within the Islamic world. It is most commonly associated with the Kharijites, an extremist sect in early Islamic history who believed in the principle of "al-irjā" (the power to decide right and wrong), and that this power lay in the hand of every Muslim, not just the caliph or religious authorities. They believed in the right of individuals to engage in self-defense and rebellion against what they perceived to be unjust rule or corrupt leaders. This ideology led to several armed rebellions and intense political upheaval in the early Islamic world. While the name "Kharijaht" has negative connotations within Islamic history, it reflects a significant period of political and societal evolution within the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Kharijaht" holds less significance than its historical and cultural impact. However, the concept of rebellion and self-defense against unjust rulers and corrupt leaders can be seen as a reflection of the larger Islamic concept of justice and the role of the individual in society. In Islamic philosophy, each person is accountable to Allah for their actions and is expected to strive towards justice and righteousness in all aspects of life. The idea that every Muslim has the power to challenge unjust rulers and seek change reflects a deeper commitment to moral and ethical principles and a belief in the inherent goodness and potential for self-improvement that exists within every individual.
